extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent applicants and practitioners (attorneys/agents) involved in appeals and post-decision prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: Official MPEP guidance on handling appeals, rehearings, reopening prosecution, withdrawals, dismissals, and related examiner/applicant actions following decisions by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB). Focused on examiner and applicant procedural obligations and time limits after Board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Reversed in Whole — immediate action
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reversal of the examiner’s rejection brings the case up for immediate action by the examiner. If the reversal does not place an application in condition for immediate allowance (e.g., Board entered a new ground of rejection under 37 CFR 41.50(b) or application contains withdrawn claims to a non-elected invention), the examiner should refer to MPEP § 1214.06 for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat reversal as routine reopening; determine whether application is in condition for allowance; consult §1214.06 when further action is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new search after reversal / give full faith to prior search
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should never regard a reversal as a challenge to make a new search to uncover other and better references. A second examiner should give full faith and credit to the prior examiner’s search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid invoking additional searches merely because a prior rejection was reversed; rely on prior examiner’s work unless specific knowledge of additional references exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization required to reopen prosecution for new references
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner has specific knowledge of the existence of particular references indicating nonpatentability of appealed claims as to which the examiner was reversed, they should submit the matter to the Technology Center (TC) Director or Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) Director for authorization to reopen prosecution under 37 CFR 1.198 to enter the new rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not unilaterally reopen prosecution to enter new rejections based on references discovered after reversal; obtain TC/CRU (and Director) authorization and place approval on the action reopening prosecution. See MPEP §§ 1002.02(c) and 1214.07.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner request for rehearing — timing and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may request rehearing of the Board decision; such a request should normally be made within 2 months of the return of the application to the TC or reexamination proceeding or reissue application to the CRU. The rehearing must state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments not raised in answers before the Board and evidence not previously relied upon are not permitted in the request for rehearing except that the examiner may present a new argument based upon a recent relevant decision of either the Board or a Federal Court. The request should set a period of 2 months for the appellant to file a reply. Rehearing requests must be approved by the TC/CRU Director and forwarded to the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy for approval before mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of claims not appealed
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 41.31(c), an appeal is presumed to be taken from the rejection of all claims. Where an appellant withdraws some appealed claims, the withdrawal is treated as an authorization to cancel the withdrawn claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must notify the appellant of cancellation of withdrawn claims. See MPEP § 1205.02. (Note: treatment differs for appeals filed before January 23, 2012 as specified.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of termination of proceedings and appellate time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings are considered terminated by dismissal of an appeal or failure to timely file a court appeal/civil action, except where claims stand allowed or further action by examiner is required. The date of termination is the date the appeal is dismissed or the time for appeal expires; the time for seeking review to the Federal Circuit or ED Va is 63 days plus any additional time granted under 37 CFR 90.3(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must ensure applications that leave Board jurisdiction are not overlooked because every case is up for action if no court review is sought. See MPEP §§ 1216.01, 1216.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: No claims stand allowed — abandonment and options for dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If no claims stand allowed after the period for seeking review expires, the application is no longer pending and a Notice of Abandonment should be prepared (or a reexamination certificate in ex parte reexamination). If dependent claims were reversed but depend on an affirmed independent claim, the examiner may either (1) convert the dependent claim into independent form by examiner’s amendment and cancel the affirmed independent claim and issue the application, or (2) set a 2-month shortened statutory period for the applicant to rewrite the dependent claim in independent form (extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) available but cannot exceed the statutory six-month maximum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no timely reply is received, the application is abandoned. Use form paragraph ¶12.291 where appropriate. Be mindful of statutory maximum reply periods (35 U.S.C. 133).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims stand allowed — issuance and handling of formal matters
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims stand allowed, the appellant is not required to file a reply. The examiner issues the application or reexamination certificate on the allowed claims and may cancel the rejected claims; if uncorrected formal matters remain that cannot be handled without correspondence, prosecution is otherwise closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If formal matters remain, set a shortened statutory period (commonly TWO (2) MONTHS) for correction to avoid abandonment; extensions under 1.136 may be available but cannot extend beyond the six-month statutory maximum. Use form paragraph ¶12.297 or ¶12.209 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims require action — non-elected species, provisional rejections, rejoinder
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board decision that reverses a rejection may bring certain claims up for action (e.g., reversal of a generic claim when non-elected species exist). Elected claims in condition for allowance require the examiner to consider claims directed to a non-elected invention for rejoinder per MPEP § 821.04. If a generic claim is reversed, pending claims to non-elected species must be acted upon unless prosecution is reopened with a new ground and election remains appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act only on matters brought up by the decision; prosecution is not open further except as to such matters. Follow MPEP § 809 and § 821.04 as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejections after Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board did not opine on a provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection but reversed other grounds as to the claim, and the applicant has not filed a proper terminal disclaimer, the examiner must act on the provisional rejection: determine if the reference application used in the provisional rejection has issued as a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reference application has issued, re-issue the provisional rejection as a non-provisional rejection and require a terminal disclaimer (use form paragraphs 8.33–8.39). If the reference application has been abandoned or has not matured to a patent and the provisional rejection is the only remaining rejection, withdraw the provisional rejection. See MPEP § 804, subsection II.B and MPEP § 1214.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 41.50(b) rejections — procedure when Board enters a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board makes a new rejection under 37 CFR 41.50(b) (a new ground), and no action is taken by appellant within 2 months, the examiner should proceed in the manner appropriate to the case (see paragraphs I–III). If the Board affirms the examiner’s rejection but also enters a new 41.50(b) ground, the subsequent procedure depends on appellant’s action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant elects to proceed before the examiner regarding the new rejection, the Board’s affirmance will be treated as nonfinal; applicant must amend claims or submit new evidence as defined in 37 CFR 41.33 (otherwise jurisdiction stays with the Board). If applicant only presents arguments without amendment/evidence, the appeal should be returned to the Board. Prosecution of a 41.50(b) rejection before the examiner can incidentally overcome an affirmed rejection and may result in allowance; if allowed, do not return to the Board. If not overcome, the applicant may file a second appeal limited to the 41.50(b) rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for rehearing of new 41.50(b) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant elects to request rehearing of the new rejection (and of the affirmance), the request for rehearing must be filed within 2 months from the date of the Board’s decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 1214.01 paragraph II and related timing rules; timeliness is strict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution after final PTAB decision — 37 CFR 1.198 authority required
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Board decision has become final for judicial review, prosecution before the primary examiner will not be reopened or reconsidered except under 37 CFR 1.114 or 37 CFR 41.50 without the written authority of the Director, and then only for consideration of matters not already adjudicated and where sufficient cause is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.198 to reopen or reconsider prosecution where no court action has been filed are decided by the Technology Center Director. See MPEP § 1002.02(c) and § 1214.07.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed after Board decision and RCE practice
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after the Board’s decision that presents new or amended claim(s) is not entered as a matter of right because prosecution is closed. However, if the amendment is submitted with an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 with the appropriate fee, prosecution will be reopened and the amendment entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE practice under 1.114 does not apply to certain utility/plant applications filed before June 8, 1995 or to design applications. If the amendment obviously places the application in condition for allowance, the primary examiner should recommend entry (with the concurrence of the supervisory patent examiner). See MPEP § 706.07(h) and § 1002.02(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to enter post-decision amendment — requirement to state reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment cannot be entered because prosecution is closed, the examiner should write to the appellant indicating that the amendment cannot be entered and stating the reason why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The refusal may not be arbitrary or capricious. Use form paragraph ¶12.298 (Amendment After Board Decision, Entry Refused) and include the date the amendment was filed and other bracketed particulars as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to reopen after court review sought (35 U.S.C. 141/145) — limited grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may entertain petitions under 37 CFR 1.198 to reopen certain cases in which an appellant has sought review under 35 U.S.C. 141 or 145, but such petitions will ordinarily be granted only in narrow categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily grant only when: (A) Board’s decision suggests a curable defect (e.g., missing disclosed limitation), (B) decision suggests required evidence exists and presently exists and can be offered, or (C) decision based on practice/rule/law/judicial precedent that has since been rescinded/repealed/overruled. Such petitions usually will not be entertained after the Director’s brief is filed in a 141 case or after trial in a 145 case. If granted, steps will be taken to request remand so proposed amendments/evidence/arguments are entered and considered by the Board or examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE practice inapplicability note
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that the RCE practice under 37 CFR 1.114 does not apply to utility or plant patent applications filed before June 8, 1995 or to design applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.114(d) and MPEP § 706.07(h), subsection I. This limitation must be observed before accepting an RCE as a basis to reopen prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of appeal — abandonment consequences and effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: Where, after an appeal has been filed and before decision by the Board, an applicant withdraws the appeal after the period for reply to the final rejection has expired, the application is to be considered abandoned as of the date on which the appeal was withdrawn unless there are allowed claims in the case. The effective date of abandonment for a letter under 37 CFR 1.138 is the date of recognition of the letter by an appropriate official or a different date if specified in the letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a brief was filed and an answer mailed and appellant withdraws prior to transfer of jurisdiction to the Board, return application to examiner. If withdrawal after jurisdiction transfer, dismissal handled by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing an RCE after notice of appeal — treated as withdrawal; must include submission and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to a decision by the Board, if applicant wishes to withdraw from appeal and reopen prosecution, filing an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 accompanied by a submission (a reply responsive to the last outstanding Office action) and the RCE fee will be treated as a withdrawal of the appeal by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An RCE without the appropriate fee or a submission in an application with no allowed claims will result in abandonment. To avoid abandonment, file the RCE in compliance with 37 CFR 1.114 and see MPEP § 706.07(h) subsections I–II. An appeal brief or reply brief is not a submission under 1.114 unless the RCE transmittal letter states it incorporates the arguments previously made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution in response to new ground in examiner’s answer or substitute answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a notice of appeal is filed, appellant may request prosecution reopened in response to a new ground of rejection made in an examiner’s answer or to a substitute examiner’s answer remanded by the Board, by filing a reply in compliance with 37 CFR 1.111 that addresses the new ground within two months from the mailing of the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1207.03 (new ground in examiner’s answer) and § 1207.05 (substitute examiner’s answer). Timely replies preserve ability to proceed before the examiner on those matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify the Board when refiling or abandoning continuations
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid the rendering of decisions by the Board in applications which have already been refiled as continuations, applicants should promptly inform the Clerk of the Board in writing as soon as they have positively decided to refile or to abandon an application containing an appeal awaiting a decision. Applicants should also advise the Board when an RCE is filed in such an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to exercise appropriate diligence may result in the Board refusing an otherwise proper request to vacate its decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial withdrawal — how to remove claims from appeal and waiver consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appellant wishes to remove claims from consideration on appeal, the appellant must submit an amendment to cancel the claims from the application. Choosing not to present arguments or rely upon particular evidence as to certain claim rejections is a waiver of those arguments/evidence for purposes of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may summarily sustain any grounds of rejection not argued. If appellant fails to respond to a new ground in an examiner’s answer or to a substitute examiner’s answer within two months, the Board will sua sponte dismiss the appeal as to the claims subject to that new ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for failure to file brief — timing and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If no brief is filed within the time prescribed by 37 CFR 41.37, the appeal stands dismissed by operation of the rule. Unless appellant specifically withdraws the appeal, do not dismiss until the extended period (up to 5 months extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a)) to file the brief has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications with no allowed claims will be abandoned. Where allowed claims remain but formal matters exist, examiner may handle them by examiner’s amendment or set a shortened statutory period (commonly TWO (2) MONTHS) for correction; use form ¶12.209 to notify applicant. Extensions under 1.136 cannot extend reply beyond the six-month statutory maximum (35 U.S.C. 133).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal because brief held non-compliant — consequences and petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal will be dismissed if an applicant fails to timely and fully reply to a notice of noncompliance under 37 CFR 41.37(d). If no allowed claims remain the application is abandoned as of the date the reply was due. If allowed claims remain, the application is not abandoned but to reinstate canceled claims/appellant must petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with a showing equivalent to a petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proper reply to the notice of noncompliance must be filed before a petition will be considered on the merits. See MPEP § 1205.03 and related authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal because required forwarding fee was not paid
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appeal forwarding fee (or other required fee related to the appeal) is not paid, the appeal may be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required fees are timely paid to avoid dismissal. (Specific fee rules and handling are described in MPEP sections following ¶1215.04 III.)
